subject: Invoice discrepancy: duplicate metering from shadow/prod traffic
messages:
From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@fastlane.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Fastlane Billing <billing@fastlane.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 17:12:00 -0400
Subject: Unexpected spike on Jul invoice - possible duplicate counting

Hi Irene / Ben,

We just received the July invoice (attached) and see a ~92% increase in billed tokens vs our internal estimate for the 7/1-7/20 window. The sample CSV you provided last month was really helpful, but this delta looks like duplicated traffic — the pattern matches times when we were running a shadowing experiment (shadowing prod requests into staging for internal QA).

Quick details:
- Account: Fastlane AI (Tenant ID: FA-3102)
- Invoice: invoice_2025-07.pdf (attached)
- Our telemetry shows the shadow flag was enabled between 7/5 01:00 UTC and 7/12 05:00 UTC and used the same API key as prod.

Can you confirm whether shadow/staging traffic is being deduplicated on your end? If the same API key was used across environments, could that have caused double-counting between prod and staging job queues? We’d like to get clarity before we process payment.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Lead Infra Engineer
Fastlane AI
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@fastlane.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on Jul invoice - possible duplicate counting

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the heads up and the attachment. I’m looping in Marissa (billing ops) and Karthik (AM) to pull the request logs and billing traces. We take duplicate-metering concerns seriously.

Quick ask while we investigate: can you send a short example of a request id and timestamp from one duplicated request pair (prod + staging) so we can trace the routing? If you can share 1–3 sample lines (request id, timestamp, endpoint, API key prefix) that’ll speed things up.

We’ll aim to confirm whether the spike is caused by attribution (single-key used across environments) or by duplicate delivery in our ingress pipeline. I’ll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the initial findings.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Rajiv Singh <rajiv@fastlane.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 11:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on Jul invoice - possible duplicate counting

Hi all,

We pulled the token-level metering around the window Rajiv mentioned. Two findings so far:
1) For tenant FA-3102 we see matched pairs of requests where the same API key prefix was used from different source IPs (likely prod vs staging). Our attribution is primarily API-key + session fingerprint; we will count each distinct incoming request unless a dedupe layer groups them.
2) We also see a small set (~1.6% of the extra tokens) that resulted from a retry loop in a batch worker on 7/9 that re-sent a subset of streaming requests.

Next steps proposed:
- If Rajiv confirms they used the same API key across environments, we can offer a one-time reconciliation credit for the duplicated time window (7/5–7/12).
- We will export the request pairs (sample) to a CSV and share tracing info; we will exclude PII.

Attaching: fastlane_sample_requests_202507.csv (sample request pairs, columns: request_id, timestamp_utc, src_ip, endpoint, token_count).

Marissa
Billing Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@fastlane.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 08:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on Jul invoice - possible duplicate counting

Thanks — confirming that we accidentally had the same API key in prod and staging for that window while toggling shadow mode (internal change failed to rotate keys). I’ve attached an example pair below (request ids and timestamps) — you should be able to find the same IDs in your logs.

Example pair (copied):
- req_7b9f2a21 , 2025-07-06T14:22:51Z , /v1/generate , key prefix: sk-FA31
- req_7b9f2a21 , 2025-07-06T14:22:51Z , /v1/generate , key prefix: sk-FA31

We appreciate an adjustment — our internal finance team needs confirmation of the credit amount and an updated invoice so we can close out July. Happy to jump on a 15-min call if needed.

— Rajiv
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@fastlane.ai>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 27 Jul 2025 09:23:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on Jul invoice - possible duplicate counting

Rajiv — thanks for the confirm and the sample. We validated the request IDs in our ingress and found clear duplicates tied to the same API key prefix and closely matched timestamps. Per our billing policy, we bill unique requests that hit our inference pipeline; because the same key hit twice from different source IPs during the shadowing window we would normally count both.

That said, given the accidental configuration on your side and the volume impact, we’re prepared to issue a one-time credit for the duplicated tokens between 2025-07-05 01:00 UTC and 2025-07-12 05:00 UTC. Proposed resolution:
- Credit amount: USD 9,420.75 (calculation attached)
- Updated invoice & statement will be posted to your Drive link within 48 hours: https://drive.google.com/fastlane/invoices/2025-07
- We’ll also open a short postmortem ticket with Engineering to add an API-key-rotation recommendation in the Manage Keys flow to prevent same-key shadowing in the future.

Please confirm if this works for Fastlane and whether you need the credit applied to this invoice or as an account credit. If you want a quick call, Ben and Karthik are available Mon 7/28 10:00-11:00 ET.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Billing Operations | Redwood Inference
